html:
The Manoki, also called Irantxe, are a small Indigenous people of Mato Grosso in western Brazil, living between the Juruena and Papagaio rivers. Their language is an isolate, with no proven relatives; the related Mỹky, a small group who split off long ago, speak almost the same tongue.

Like the Aikanã and others of the region, they lost many people to epidemics once outsiders arrived in the 1900s, during and after the rubber boom. Missionaries took many children to boarding schools, and the language is now spoken mostly by elders. They farm, hunt and fish on a small reserve.
